name: Brixton
fact_sentence: One in three residents here was born outside the UK — Portuguese, Spanish, and Yoruba spoken in the same market.
history_sentence: Brixton station opened in 1971 as the southern terminus of the Victoria Line, the last major tube extension of the twentieth century.

name: Stockwell
fact_sentence: The largest Portuguese-speaking community in Britain lives within walking distance of this platform.
history_sentence: Stockwell opened with the Victoria Line in 1971 and sits above a deep interchange that locals call 'the spaghetti junction of the south'.

name: Vauxhall
fact_sentence: A ten-storey building opposite the station houses the Secret Intelligence Service — GCHQ's London address, visible to everyone.
history_sentence: Vauxhall's Victorian Pleasure Gardens drew Londoners for two centuries before the station arrived in 1971; the river remembers both.

name: Pimlico
fact_sentence: Pimlico's white stucco terraces were built on marshland reclaimed by Thomas Cubitt in the 1820s — the wealth was planned, not accumulated.
history_sentence: Pimlico is the only Victoria Line station with no interchange, the quietest stop between Brixton and Victoria, a secret in plain sight.

name: Victoria
fact_sentence: Over 80 million passengers pass through Victoria station annually — one of the most transited places on earth, where London briefly holds its breath.
history_sentence: Victoria tube station opened in 1969, two years before the line reached Brixton; the south had to wait a little longer, as it often does.

name: Green Park
fact_sentence: The median property price within five minutes of this exit exceeds £3 million — the most expensive earth in England, directly above the platforms.
history_sentence: Green Park station opened in 1969; the park above has no flowerbeds by royal decree, a tradition since Queen Caroline tore them up in the 1730s.

name: Oxford Circus
fact_sentence: Oxford Circus is the busiest interchange on the entire Underground network, recording over 200,000 entries and exits on a typical weekday.
history_sentence: The diagonal crossing at street level above — four simultaneous pedestrian streams — was installed in 2009, modelled on Shibuya in Tokyo.

name: Warren Street
fact_sentence: Three major teaching hospitals stand within half a mile of Warren Street — University College Hospital, the National Hospital, and the Eastman Dental.
history_sentence: Warren Street station was named after a nearby street, which was itself named after Sir Peter Warren, an eighteenth-century admiral and speculator.

name: Euston
fact_sentence: The original Euston Arch — a vast Doric propylaeum — was demolished in 1961 despite public outcry; its ghost is still argued over.
history_sentence: Euston's Victoria Line platforms opened in 1968, part of the first stretch to run; the station has been half-demolished and rebuilt in every decade since.

name: King's Cross St. Pancras
fact_sentence: Six Underground lines converge here, along with Eurostar, the East Coast Main Line, and Thameslink — the largest underground station complex in Europe.
history_sentence: For decades the King's Cross area was one of London's least loved districts; the regeneration of the Goods Yard, completed in the 2010s, remade it almost entirely.

name: Highbury & Islington
fact_sentence: Islington has more restaurants per resident than any other London borough, and more people on waiting lists for social housing than almost any other.
history_sentence: Highbury & Islington joined the Victoria Line in 1968; the station sits beneath an overground interchange that predates the tube by a century.

name: Finsbury Park
fact_sentence: The Finsbury Park mosque is one of the largest in Britain; within a quarter mile, Eritrean, Turkish, and Kurdish communities have each built something permanent.
history_sentence: Finsbury Park station opened in 1968 and has remained stubbornly ungentrified despite the surrounding postcode rising around it — a junction that resists tidying.

name: Seven Sisters
fact_sentence: Seven Sisters has one of the highest proportions of Latin American residents in London — a community built quietly over forty years.
history_sentence: The station opened in 1968; the name comes from seven elms that once marked the common, all felled long before the first train arrived.

name: Tottenham Hale
fact_sentence: Tottenham Hale ward has one of the twenty highest deprivation scores in England — a figure that sits three miles and thirty minutes from Green Park.
history_sentence: Tottenham Hale opened with the Victoria Line's northern extension in 1968, giving the Lee Valley its first direct connection to the West End.

name: Blackhorse Road
fact_sentence: Artist studios, craft breweries, and Walthamstow Wetlands — one of Europe's largest urban nature reserves — converge within ten minutes of this exit.
history_sentence: Blackhorse Road station opened in 1968; the street it sits on was named for a public house that stood here for three hundred years before the tube arrived.

name: Walthamstow Central
fact_sentence: William Morris was born here in 1834; Europe's longest outdoor street market still runs daily along the high road he would have walked.
history_sentence: Walthamstow Central became the northern terminus of the Victoria Line in 1968, the final station in the original plan — the end of the line, for now.
